ASEAN tigers regain their bite
**Delivering commercial insight** **www.woodmac.com** # **ASEAN tigers regain their bite** **China has been a major driver of global copper demand over the past decade but at the same time other Asian countries have been gradually increasing in importance. This** **_Insight_ investigates the growth to date of key ASEAN consumers, illustrates their structural drivers and forecasts future copper demand growth prospects.** **Consumption of refined copper in Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia and Vietnam has grown from a combined 456kt in 2001 to 743kt in 2011 and now accounts for c.4% of global refined demand.** **In this presentation we also reveal “real” demand for copper, which considers the direct use of scrap and net trade in semi-fabricated products and wire and cable.** **The charts in the following slides highlight the clear underlying relationships between demand for copper, economic development, electricity consumption and urbanisation. Continued growth in these factors at the same time as inward investment in OEM components and finished goods will boost demand through the medium to long term.** **The ASEAN Free Trade Area was formed in 1992 with the objective of increasing the region’s competiveness through the elimination of tariff and non-tariff barriers within the zone and to encourage investment into the area. The original members of Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand were later joined by Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar and Cambodia.** 2 **Delivering commercial insight** **www.woodmac.com** # **As countries become richer they consume more copper, up to a point** 50,000

5 **Delivering commercial insight** **www.woodmac.com** # **Indonesia** **Economic growth in Indonesia has been bolstered largely by high private consumption growth and investment, offsetting relatively weaker export growth. Private consumption and investment are the main engines of growth, accounting for 60% and 30% of the economy respectively. This makes Indonesia less vulnerable to external conditions given its deep local market, while exports only make up 24% of its GDP.** **It has been the investment element of economic growth in Indonesia which has been particularly beneficial to copper demand. Infrastructure projects were a boon to cable makers in the first half of 2012, boosting demand by 15-20% yoy.** **There was, however, a slowdown in demand in the second half of the year. Despite it being less reliant on exports as a component of GDP, as a component of total copper demand they account for around a third of consumption. It was external weakness that slowed demand in H2 2012.** |**Vital statistics**|**2000**|**2005**|**2011**| |---|---|---|---| |GDP growth|5%|6%|6%| |IP growth|17%|9%|4%| |Refined Cu consumption (kt)|151|241|210| |Real Cu consumption (kt)|84|86|161| |Population (m)|213|227|242| |Urbanised population|42%|46%|51%| |Refined Cu per capita (kg)|0.3|0.9|0.9| |Real Cu per capita (kg)|0.4|0.4|0.7| |Electricityconsumption(ktoe)|6808|9205|13515| **_ktoe = kilotonnes of oil equivalent_** 6 **Delivering commercial insight** **www.woodmac.com** # **Rod dominates downstream capacity in Indonesia** **Wire rod almost exclusively accounts for refined consumption in Indonesia.** **There are a large number of wire and cable companies, ranging in size, many of which have their own rod line.** **Mines/Smelters/Refiners Cable makers with own rod line Wire and cable makers** PT Freeport Tembaga Mulia Semanan Sumi Indo Kabel Newmont Mining Karya Sumiden Indonesia Sumitomo Electric Wintec PT Smelting Supreme Cable Kabelindo Murni KMI Wire and Cable Tranka Kabel Jembo Cable Prysmian Cable Indonesia Prima Cable Indo **Associatio

# **Investment and infrastructure underpin Indonesian outlook** **As we noted in our introduction, investment and infrastructure account for a large share of Indonesian copper demand and we forecast that this will continue to drive consumption.** **Indonesia is a large country and its urbanisation will be partly behind the need for the expansion of urban copper power distribution networks. Meanwhile, the current focus on the mining industry will likely support infrastructure spending.** **Demand will also be lifted by investment in OEM component plants, such as for wiring harnesses. We believe that this will be to a lesser extent than in other Asian neighbours such as Thailand, which have quickly established supply chains.** **One sector likely to temper growth is telecom, which is set to face the same negative headwind that has befallen Western countries of the penetration of fibre optic cable replacing copper telecom cable.** kt

9 **Delivering commercial insight** |**www.woodmac.com**| |---| # **Thailand** **Economic growth bounced back in 2012 following the disruptions of the prior year from the large scale flooding. Exports play a major role in Thai economic activity and despite the relative weakness of neighbouring markets, the base effect of 2011 resulted in a rebound in activity this year.** **Whereas the build out of energy infrastructure was behind growth in Indonesian copper demand, in Thailand, consumption has been driven in large part by the relocation of foreign OEM component plants. Japanese companies in particular have been at the forefront of this, although by no means exclusively.** **The floods in Thailand put a real dampener on refined copper consumption at the end of 2011, and despite a strong sequential recovery at the start of 2012, yearon-year growth was still down on the prior year in Q1. Some of this demand was met by imports of semis. The second and third quarters improved sequentially and we expect demand to be significantly higher for the full year.** |**Vital statistic

13 **Delivering commercial insight** |**www.woodmac.com**| |---| # **Malaysia** **Malaysia has a high export to GDP ratio of nearly 100%, indicating the extent of dependence on external trade. As a result we expect private consumption and business investment to remain the main drivers of growth in the short-term. The relative resilience of the labour market and healthy pay rises for civil servants will help underpin consumer confidence and domestic spending.** **Most of the development of semis capacity in Malaysia has been as a result of investment by domestic companies, although at the same time much of this has been to serve the export market.** **The year started off well for Malaysia although activity slowed sharply into the second quarter. 17 **Delivering commercial insight** # **Vietnam** **Economic expansion is largely driven by the manufacturing and services sectors. Private consumption and exports make up about two-thirds of GDP making them the key drivers of growth. The pace of economic activity slowed slightly in 2012, reflecting weakening external conditions as well as the domestic challenges of managing inflation, the trade deficit and maintaining economic growth.** **Percentage growth rates for copper demand in Vietnam look impressive at first glance although clearly this was from a standing start. Arguably, the pace of development could have occurred much more quickly given that the first major rod line with a capacity of 80kta went into production over a decade ago.** **Growth to date has been largely driven by domestic demand from wire and cable makers with rod production accounting almost exclusively for refined demand.** **After steady growth in 2011, demand looks set for another year of muted activity in 2012 despite a sharp increase in activity in the first part of the year.** |**Vital statistics**|**2000**|**2005**|**2011**| |---|---|---|---| |GDP growth|6.8%|8.4%|5.9%| |IP growth|12.7%|12.1%|6.0%| |Refined Cu consumption (kt)|17|70|100| |Real Cu Consumption (kt)|31|69|142| |Population (m)|79|83|89| |Urbanised population|24%|27%|27%| |Refined Cu per capita (kg)|0.2|0.8|1.1| |Real Cu per capita (kg)|0.4|0.8|1.6| |Electricityconsumption(ktoe)|1991|4748|9296| ### **_ktoe = kilotonnes of oil equivalent_** 18 **Delivering commercial insight** **www.woodmac.com** # **Downstream capacity in Vietnam** **Rod almost exclusively accounts for domestic semis capacity** **Current semis and downstream capacity has been a combination of overseas and domestic investment with CFT Vina Copper, by far the largest rod maker, a JV with a Japanese firm. 20 **Delivering commercial insight** **www.woodmac.com** # **Inward investment set to drive growth in Vietnam** **Although the pace of growth has been slower than expected so far, we remain bullish on the outlook. Importantly, because we are at a higher base, lower percentage growth rates still result in healthy volumes of metal.** **Vietnam is expected to be a major source of future demand growth in part owing to its stage of economic development but it is also helped by demographic drivers. It has a large population of c.90m and a relatively low rate of urbanisation. Also, its ports and location are favourable for trade. These factors combined make Vietnam an attractive location for inward investment as a result of plentiful supply of cheap labour.** **Growth will be driven by further industrialisation of the country as OEMs move operations to Vietnam. At the same time this will lead to an increased call on infrastructure investment. A combination of these two factors will drive income growth which will result in increasing demand for consumer goods, further lifting copper consumption.** kt

**Source: Wood Mackenzie** 21 **Delivering commercial insight** **www.woodmac.com** # **Summary** **The four ASEAN countries in this presentation have a number of structural pluses in their favour and this will drive demand for copper over the medium to long term. These pluses include:** - Developing economies, large populations and low wages make these countries attractive for inward investment and this will lead to OEMs shifting production to these locations - Inward and domestic investment will support income growth and increased urbanisation spurring building and construction as well as demand for consumer goods - Rising personal wealth and investment will result in greater demand for electricity and will drive a requirement for further electrical infrastructure investment and distribution equipment **These factors will combine to drive annual refined copper demand growth at an average pace of 5.8% over the next five years, well above the total global growth forecast.** |||||||**2016 vs 2011**
